title: Common Nutrition Myths Debunked

authorship.current_visible_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team
authorship.recommended_normalized_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team

primary_question: Which common nutrition claims are myths, and what does the evidence actually say?
reader_intent: Replace ten common nutrition myths (carbs, fat, detox, meal timing, sugar, meal frequency, gluten, superfoods, supplements, calorie equivalence) with accurate framing.
desired_reader_outcome: Reader can evaluate nutrition claims critically and knows evidence-based positions on ten specific common myths.

claims.proposition: Meal frequency has minimal impact on metabolism; the thermic effect of food is proportional to total calorie intake, not meal count.
claims.recommended_action: Consistent with claim-metabolic-rate-stable-20-to-60's general metabolic-stability framing and standard nutrition science; zero citation given.

claims.proposition: Gluten-free diets provide no general health benefit for people without celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
claims.recommended_action: Standard, well-established nutrition-science consensus position; zero citation given.

internal_link_recommendations.reason: Shares the meal-frequency/metabolism myth; cross-linking would help readers see the fuller treatment.

disposition_reason: Broad, genuinely distinct scope (ten myths spanning multiple nutrition domains, broader than any single overlapping article) with reasonable, well-established positions, but zero sources anywhere across ten separate factual claims.
required_research: Cite representative primary/consensus sources for each of the ten myths, prioritizing the ones with the most specific factual content (gluten, meal timing, meal frequency).
recommended_rewrite_scope: Add a Sources section covering the range of topics addressed.
